# Instructions for accurately documenting failed brake tests in a vehicle inspection report

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
2. Record the date and time of the inspection.
3. Enter the vehicle’s identification details, including make, model, year, VIN, registration number, and mileage.
4. List the components of the brake system that were inspected, such as the brake pads, rotors, calipers, lines, and ABS system.
5. Use standardized checklists to ensure all aspects of the brake system are included in the inspection.
6. Note any visual observations before conducting the actual brake tests (e.g., oil or brake fluid leaks, signs of excessive wear, or missing components).
7. Document the procedures used for testing the brakes; this may include a pressure test, measurement of pad thickness, rotor wear, and operation of the ABS system.
8. Clearly indicate each test conducted and the result (e.g., Pass/Fail).
9. If a brake test failure occurs, describe the failed test in detail, including:
